notes.summary: New draft theorem: every finite-valued function satisfying the printed rational-endpoint PC inequalities on a finite positive balanced rational space has a unique continuous PC representative agreeing at rational points and dominating it everywhere. The representative is its upper semicontinuous hull. No boundedness or continuity premise is imposed on the original function; no PA regularization or MA extension follows.
notes.detailedSummary: The proof reconstructs positive spanning of every balanced local star, a uniform finite-generator representation bound, two exact rational PCC estimates, and automatic local bounds on rational values. These yield compatible continuous extensions across shared faces and irrational centers. A rational perspective-polyhedron argument proves PCC inequalities with real endpoints for the completion. The origin of a finite rational fan has rational-value continuity for every printed-PC function exactly when its generated cone equals its span; this origin criterion does not control other unbalanced stars. These are mathematical proof claims in an unverified draft, not conclusions certified by finite computation.
notes.text:
Conventions and statement. Let X be the support of a finite rational polyhedral complex Π in V=N⊗R, and let X_Q=X∩(N⊗Q). A printed PCC has rational endpoints x_i, real nonnegative coefficients α_i summing to one, and center x=Σα_i x_i. On some rational carrying structure there are faces τ⊆σ_i with x∈τ and x_i∈σ_i. PC_q means the real-valued functions satisfying every such Jensen inequality; continuity is not included. PA_Z means continuous finite PA functions with integral tangent slopes and rational affine constants. PA_R separately means arbitrary real affine coefficients on a finite rational structure. Uniform decreasing PA regularization remains a separate requirement in either category.

The theorem proved here is: if every local star of Π is positively spanning, every finite-valued q∈PC_q(X) has a unique F∈C(X) agreeing with q on X_Q. Moreover q≤F, F satisfies every corresponding real-endpoint PCC inequality on every rational carrying structure, and F(x)=limsup_{y→x}q(y). It is the least continuous majorant of q. Conversely, any finite-valued q agreeing with such an F on X_Q and satisfying q≤F belongs to PC_q. Positive balancing implies the geometric hypothesis in every dimension. The original q can remain discontinuous and can be unbounded below on irrational points.

Uniform star geometry. For τ⊆σ put C_{σ/τ}={t(a−b):t≥0,a∈σ,b∈τ}. At z∈relint(τ), this is the tangent cone of σ and includes the lineality span(τ−τ). Write σ using rational affine equations and inequalities A_jx≥b_j. The inequalities active at z are precisely those active on all of τ. On a compact K⊂relint(τ), every other inequality has a uniform positive slack. Consequently there is a uniform radius r such that z+d∈σ whenever z∈K, d belongs to the active-inequality tangent cone, and ||d||<r. Conversely y−z lies in that cone for every y∈σ. This also proves equality with the displayed C_{σ/τ}: for an allowed tangent vector d, a sufficiently small z+td∈σ gives d=t^{-1}((z+td)−z).

Each rational cone has a finite rational generating list, including a basis and its negatives for lineality. To justify this directly, quotient its rational lineality. The sum of its defining inequality forms is strictly positive on the resulting pointed cone away from zero. Its section at value one is a bounded rational polytope. Moving in the kernel of active constraints in both directions expresses any nonvertex point as a convex combination of points with more independent active constraints; boundedness gives endpoints and iteration terminates at vertices. Each vertex solves a rational full-rank system. Lifting those rays and adding the lineality generators supplies the required list.

Take the union v_1,…,v_m of the local cone lists, recording each incident-face assignment. A positive rational ε can be chosen uniformly over K so that z+εv_i lies in every face to which v_i is assigned. There is also a common C such that every d in any one local cone has a representation d=Σa_i v_i, a_i≥0, using that cone's generators, with Σa_i≤C||d||. Indeed eliminate dependent active columns: for a nonzero relation Σb_i v_i=0, change its sign to have a positive entry and subtract min_{b_i>0}(a_i/b_i) times the relation. This preserves nonnegativity and removes an active column. An independent subset remains. Its coefficients are a linear inverse of its column map and thus have an l1 bound C_T||d||. There are finitely many subsets. For rational d, the independent rational system gives rational coefficients by Gaussian elimination.

Positive spanning means that the cone generated by the local support equals its linear span. This is equivalent to a relation Σλ_i v_i=0 with every λ_i positive rational. One direction expresses each −v_i using the positive relation. For the reverse direction express each −v_i nonnegatively using the generators, make these representations rational by the preceding elimination, and add all relations v_i+Σb_ij v_j=0. Every resulting coefficient is at least one.

Why positive balancing supplies this condition. Use saturated tangent lattices N_σ=N∩span_R(σ−σ) and primitive inward normal classes n_{σ/δ} in N_σ/N_δ. The weights w_σ>0 satisfy Σw_σ n_{σ/δ}∈N_{δ,R}. The star inherits these lattices, normal classes, and weights: the active-inequality description preserves tangent spaces and inward facet signs.

For a positive balanced fan choose a Euclidean inner product and let a_σ be the covolume of N_σ in its tangent space. The perpendicular height of a primitive inward normal is a_σ/a_δ, because a basis of the saturated facet lattice followed by that normal is a basis of N_σ. Thus c_σ=w_σa_σ and the inward unit conormals satisfy Σc_σν_{σ/δ}=0. Ordinary divergence on each cell, with facet cancellation, gives Σc_σ∫_σ div_σY=0 for every compactly supported C1 ambient vector field. Unbounded cells may be truncated beyond its support. These auxiliary Euclidean weights are not MA weights.

Apply this identity to Y(x)=bχ(||x||), where χ is smooth, nonincreasing, one near zero, zero far away, and decreasing on an interval. Polar integration gives zero weighted angular barycenter, because the radial factor ∫χ′(r)r^{d−1}dr is strictly negative. A linear form nonnegative on the support and positive somewhere would have a positive angular integral on a relatively open subset of a top cone, contradicting that barycenter. The generated cone is closed: independent-column representations of a convergent sequence have bounded coefficients, and a subsequence with a fixed active subset converges to a representation of the limit. If the cone D were proper in its span, choose y outside D and its nearest point p∈D. The projection inequality gives <p−y,z−p>≥0 for z∈D; z=0,2p gives <p−y,p>=0. Hence ℓ(z)=<p−y,z> is nonnegative on D but ℓ(y)=−||p−y||²<0. Since the support spans the ambient span of D, ℓ must be positive somewhere on the support, a contradiction. Dimension zero needs no generators. This reconstructs the needed balancing geometry without importing automatic continuity.

Two exact rational PCC estimates. Fix rational z∈K and rational y∈σ⊇τ, set d=y−z, and choose rational a_i as above with A=Σa_i≤ε. Set z_i=z+εv_i. The equality y=(1−A/ε)z+Σ(a_i/ε)z_i is a PCC centered in σ after omitting indices a_i=0. Every retained endpoint lies in σ. Therefore q(y)−q(z)≤Σ(a_i/ε)(q(z_i)−q(z)). Omitting these zero terms constructs a valid PCC; it does not alter the printed weak definition.

For the reverse estimate set t=max_i(a_i/λ_i) and b_i=(tλ_i−a_i)/ε≥0. Then d+Σb_iεv_i=0. Thus z is the PCC of y with unnormalized coefficient one and of the z_i with coefficients b_i. Its center is in τ and all endpoint faces contain τ. Rearranging Jensen gives q(y)≥q(z)+Σb_i(q(z)−q(z_i)). Writing Λ=Σλ_i and λ_min=min λ_i, we have B=Σb_i≤H||d||, where H=CΛ/(ελ_min). If all rational values used are between m_0 and M_0, both inequalities give |q(y)−q(z)|≤(M_0−m_0)L||y−z||, where L=(C/ε)max(1,Λ/λ_min).

Automatic rational bounds. At any possibly irrational p∈relint(τ), choose a compact relative neighborhood K and its uniform geometry. A small neighborhood of p meets only faces containing τ, since the complex is finite and its other faces are closed. Choose one fixed rational anchor z∈K close enough to p and then a small neighborhood W so that C||y−z||≤ε for y∈W. The finite values q(z),q(z_i) have a finite maximum M. The upper PCC bounds every rational q(y) in W by M. The lower PCC gives q(y)≥q(z)−H||y−z||(M−q(z)), a uniform finite lower bound on a bounded smaller W. No lower bound or continuity of the original q was assumed. Isolated rational points use their own finite values.

Completion and face compatibility. The rational endpoint sets z+εv_i for z in a compact relative neighborhood form compact subsets of X. A finite cover by the preceding local rational bounds supplies common m_0,M_0 for those sets and nearby rational centers. The transverse estimate is therefore uniform as rational z varies in that neighborhood. Within relint(τ), it gives a local Lipschitz bound on rational values and consequently a unique continuous extension F_τ there.

For an arbitrary rational sequence y_n→p through incident faces, choose rational z_n∈relint(τ) tending to p. The uniform estimate gives q(y_n)−q(z_n)→0, so every rational sequence approaching p has the same limit F_τ(p). This establishes shared-face compatibility, including at irrational p, and defines F throughout X. For rational y near p, let rational z in τ approach p in the estimate to obtain |q(y)−F(p)|≤(M_0−m_0)L||y−p||. Then let rational y approach any nearby real p′, using its already established unique rational limit. This proves continuity of F in the full topology. Uniqueness follows from rational density.

To prove q(x)≤F(x) at an irrational center, enclose x in successively smaller rational coordinate boxes within the relative interior of its rational face and triangulate. A simplex containing x has rational vertices r_j and expresses x barycentrically. It is an actual PCC with center and endpoints in that face. Hence q(x)≤Σα_jq(r_j)=Σα_jF(r_j)→F(x). Agreement holds at rational points.

All real-endpoint PCC inequalities. Fix any rational carrying structure and any real-endpoint PCC with faces τ⊆σ_i. Discard zero-coefficient endpoints. Write the rational constraints of σ_i as A_ix_i≥b_i, with equations included, and introduce t_i=α_i x_i. The conditions α_i≥0, Σα_i=1, A_it_i≥b_iα_i, and Σt_i∈τ define a rational polyhedron. Rational points are dense in the minimal face of any feasible point: solve all its active rational constraints by Gaussian elimination, use a rational affine basis, and approximate its coordinates; inactive inequalities remain strict. Approximate the given perspective variables rationally. Retained coefficients stay positive, so x_i^(n)=t_i^(n)/α_i^(n) are rational points in σ_i and x^(n)=Σt_i^(n) is rational in τ. Apply q's actual PCC inequalities, replace rational q values by F values, and pass to the limit using continuity. This proves every real-endpoint inequality with all face constraints preserved.

Finally q≤F and continuity give q*≤F, while rational sequences give q*≥F. Any continuous majorant of q majorizes F on rational points and hence everywhere. Conversely, if q≤F and agrees at rational points, every printed PCC satisfies q(x)≤F(x)≤Σα_iF(x_i)=Σα_iq(x_i).

Sharpness at a fan vertex. On a finite rational fan, every finite-valued PC_q function has rational values continuous at the origin if and only if cone(X)=span_R(X). Sufficiency uses the two estimates at z=0 and the automatic rational bounds there; subdivide rational lineality if needed to make zero a vertex. Necessity: if the generated cone is proper, separate it by ℓ≥0 on X and positive somewhere. The function q=0 on ℓ=0 and q=−1 on ℓ>0 satisfies even real-endpoint Jensen, but q(v/n)=−1 for a rational generator with ℓ(v)>0 while q(0)=0.

Origin spanning alone is insufficient for global completion. The unbalanced fan consisting of the positive and negative quadrants in R² spans R², but its star at (1,0) is a half-plane. Define q(x,0)=x for x≥0, q(x,y)=0 for x≥0,y>0, and q(x,y)=−x on the negative quadrant. At a negative-quadrant center, q equals the ambient linear form −x, which it majorizes globally. At a positive center with y>0, or at zero, its value is zero and all endpoint values are nonnegative. At a positive horizontal center, an incident-face endpoint with negative second coordinate is impossible because the connecting segment would leave X; the barycenter therefore forces active endpoints onto the horizontal axis, where q=|x| is convex. Thus all PCC inequalities hold, yet rational values jump at (1,0). This diagnostic lies outside the positive balanced domain.

Exact finite evidence, separate from the proof: check_star_estimates.py passed all 1,035 specified barycentric cases and 2,070 convex-function cases. The cross, fine U(3,4), and translated trivalent counts were respectively 36/72, 972/1,944, and 27/54. These results exhaust only the supplied rational grids, not a continuum theorem or operator-domain test. Full proofs and evidence are retained in P05.2-paper.tex, P05.2-paper.pdf, argument.md, notes.json, star-input.json, and evidence/star-check-output.json. The original contact classification is not claimed.

notes.summary: Using n1, the unrestricted printed envelope is continuous and equals the continuous-competitor envelope for every bounded continuous obstacle on every finite positive balanced space. This includes all PA obstacles in each separately fixed coefficient category. General noncompact PA regularization and MA contact remain unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: The finite printed-PC supremum lies between gamma+inf(u) and gamma+u. Its completion preserves the continuous obstacle and uniform global growth bounds from rational points, so it is itself an original competitor and must equal the envelope. Each original competitor also has a valid continuous completion. A separate compact category with compatible integral-affine rational charts has exact component-minimum envelopes over unrestricted competitors; finite bounded literal data give rational constant PA endpoints, constant decreasing regularizations, and zero chartwise raw iterated-divisor measure in positive dimension. No arbitrary continuous endpoint receives an unsupported MA measure.
notes.text:
All-obstacle envelope theorem. Let X satisfy the completion theorem n1, let γ∈PC_c(X) be continuous, and let u∈C_b(X). Define P(x)=sup{q(x):q∈PC_q(X), q≤γ+u, q≤γ+C_q globally for some real C_q}. Then P is finite, continuous, satisfies real-endpoint PCC inequalities, equals the supremum over continuous PC competitors, and equals its upper semicontinuous regularization. Moreover γ+inf_Xu≤P≤γ+u≤γ+sup_Xu, and ||P_γ(u)−P_γ(v)||∞≤||u−v||∞. Positive growth is not required for this continuity result.

Proof. The continuous PC function γ+inf_Xu is a competitor, giving the lower bound and nonemptiness. The obstacle gives a finite upper bound. A finite supremum of this family is printed PC directly: for a permitted PCC, every competitor satisfies q(x)≤Σα_iq(x_i)≤Σα_iP(x_i); take the supremum at the center. Apply n1 to this finite-valued P. Its completion F agrees on rational points and dominates P. The continuous obstacle and γ+sup_Xu bound F at rational points and therefore everywhere. Thus F is a valid competitor in the original unrestricted supremum. Maximality gives P≥F, hence P=F. This proves continuity without assuming continuity of any original competitor.

There is also a direct competitor identification: the completion F_q of each original q passes both q≤γ+u and q≤γ+C_q from rational points to all points. It is a continuous competitor dominating q, with its actual global growth constraint preserved. Consequently the two competitor envelopes agree. For nonexpansiveness set a=||u−v||∞. Monotonicity and addition of constants give P_γ(u)≤P_γ(v+a)=P_γ(v)+a; reverse u,v for the other bound. These are elementary printed Jensen operations, not PA closure or regularization assertions.

This theorem covers every bounded obstacle in PA_Z and separately every bounded obstacle in PA_R on every finite positive balanced rational space. It also covers arbitrary nonseparable product obstacles for continuity. It does not show P∈PA_R, P∈PC_reg,R, literal regularization, or a genuine extended MA domain.

Compact embedded/category boundary. A nonempty finite globally embedded positive balanced cycle of dimension d≥1 cannot have compact support. The covolume-weighted divergence cancellation proved in n1 applies to a finite complex. If the support were compact, a compactly supported vector field equal to Y(x)=x near it would give 0=dΣw_σa_σ vol_d(σ)>0. Thus compact locally charted spaces must be named separately.

Unrestricted compact-chart conclusion. Let X be compact with locally embedded rational polyhedral charts, compatible positive balanced weights, and integral-affine lattice-isomorphism transition maps with rational translation. Use printed local PCC inequalities for its PC class. The completion proof is local: choose every star endpoint within the chart. Chart transitions identify rational points, so local continuous completions agree on the dense rational overlap and glue. The perspective argument gives the real-endpoint local inequalities.

Every continuous PC function F is constant on each connected component. Indeed, at a maximum p with value M, use a positive star relation and represent any nearby real displacement y−p=Σa_iv_i. The lower-combination construction in n1 expresses p as a real-endpoint PCC of y and p+εv_i, with a strictly positive coefficient at y. All values are at most M, so Jensen forces F(y)=M. The maximum set is open and closed. Polyhedral chart spaces are locally connected, hence their components are open; compactness gives finitely many compact components and a maximum on each. The conclusion follows.

For continuous PC γ and continuous u on this compact category, every original printed competitor q has a continuous completion F_q below γ+u. On a component D it is a constant at most min_D(γ+u), and it dominates q. Conversely the componentwise constants min_D(γ+u) are continuous PC competitors. Therefore the actual unrestricted envelope is exactly P_γ(u)|D=min_{x∈D}(γ(x)+u(x)). The continuous maximum principle is applied only after establishing the actual representative.

Genuine finite PA endpoints. If γ,u are literal PA on a finite bounded rational carrying decomposition compatible with these charts, every cellwise affine obstacle minimum is attained at a rational vertex and has a rational value. Thus the component minima are rational constants, and the envelope is literal PA. A constant sequence, or addition of decreasing positive rational constants, is a valid decreasing uniform literal regularization. In the separately declared real category the constants may be real; they are real PA and have the same direct regularization.

For this separate chart category use the raw recursive divisor formula with saturated primitive inward normal classes and compatible cycle weights. For a constant k and balanced cycle c, (k·c)(τ)=Σ_{σ≻τ}c(σ)k_σ(n_{σ/τ})−k_τ(Σ_{σ≻τ}c(σ)n_{σ/τ})=0 because every linear part vanishes. The zero coefficients agree on overlapping integral-affine charts, so the first divisor is the global zero cycle and every subsequent divisor is zero. Thus in positive dimension this finite PA endpoint has zero raw iterated-divisor measure and exact contact integral zero. No extra factorial is inserted, and no general continuous operator extension is used.

In dimension zero a globally embedded finite rational space is a finite set of rational points. PCCs are confined to singleton faces, the exact envelope is γ+u, and the genuine zero-fold measure is the given weighted cycle. Its contact gap is identically zero. These scoped conclusions do not classify positive-dimensional noncompact contact.

The complete arguments are in P05.2-paper.tex, P05.2-paper.pdf and argument.md. No raw MA is assigned here to the merely continuous noncompact envelopes.

notes.summary: New diagnostic: gamma on rational points and gamma−1 elsewhere is printed PC with exact uniform distance 1/2 from all continuous functions. Entire printed-PC density/equality therefore fail in both coefficient categories, independently of continuous-envelope regularizability. The full P05.2 classification remains open; the paper, PDF, structured notes, source ledger and reproducible evidence were produced.
notes.detailedSummary: The approximation gap follows from rational sequences approaching an irrational point inside a positive-dimensional rational cell. It prevents uniform density of either PA category in the full printed PC class and equality with uniform PA limits. It does not exhibit a nonregularizable continuous-obstacle envelope. The new completion and unrestricted-envelope results resolve that antecedent across all finite positive balanced spaces, while global PA approximation, genuine extended MA domains, structural local contact and global reference-compatible realization remain unresolved. Final candidate status is false. The PDF has 13 pages and a clean final build; finite computation and compilation are evidence observations only.
notes.text:
Quantitative entire-class obstruction. Let X contain a positive-dimensional rational cell and let γ∈PC_c(X). Define q_γ(x)=γ(x) on X_Q and q_γ(x)=γ(x)−1 elsewhere. For every printed PCC, q_γ(x)≤γ(x)≤Σα_iγ(x_i)=Σα_iq_γ(x_i), because the endpoints are rational. Hence q_γ is printed PC and differs boundedly from γ.

Its exact uniform distance from C(X) is 1/2. Choose an irrational p in the relative interior of a positive-dimensional rational cell and rational r_n→p. If continuous f has uniform error δ, comparison at r_n and continuity imply f(p)≥γ(p)−δ. Comparison at p gives f(p)≤γ(p)−1+δ. Therefore δ≥1/2. The continuous function γ−1/2 attains error exactly 1/2. Every PA function and every uniform PA limit is continuous. Consequently neither PA_Z∩PC_q nor PA_R∩PC_q is uniformly dense in the whole bounded-relative printed PC class, and that entire class cannot equal either decreasing uniform PA regularizable class.

This is a distinction between entire-class density and endpoint regularity. The source's Theorem 6.4 connects all-PA-obstacle regularization with density and equality statements involving its PC class. Those latter statements cannot be treated as already checked consequences of continuity under the printed rational-endpoint reading. The original endpoint antecedent must instead be checked directly in each coefficient category: P_γ(u) belongs to PC_reg,* for every admissible u, followed by a genuine MA operator and the exact contact integral. The discontinuity of q_γ does not show failure at a continuous-obstacle envelope; its completion is γ, and n2 proves the actual envelope is continuous.

Precise remaining original scope. No necessary-and-sufficient structural contact classification was obtained. The unresolved requirements include global PA approximation with the actual reference growth in each coefficient category, genuine extended MA domains at every admissible envelope, an adequate higher-dimensional local raw-contact criterion, and proof that its necessity and sufficiency survive global endpoint realization for all obstacles. Continuity does not supply these premises. No raw measure has been assigned to an unsupported endpoint. The accepted A224 obstruction is retained as context under exactly its granted scope; it is not promoted to real pair-level regularity or claimed as new work. The needed B225 geometry was reconstructed in n1 rather than applying its continuous maximum principle before obtaining a representative. A224 and B225 are caller grants, not invented registered note IDs.

Failed methods retained. Declaring every original rational-endpoint PC function continuous fails because arbitrary downward changes away from the rational locus preserve all printed inequalities. Using positive spanning only at a fan origin fails to control its other stars, as the explicit unbalanced two-quadrant example in n1 demonstrates. Declaring a continuous envelope regularizable, or applying an extended MA operator solely because it is continuous, omits the required global approximation and operator-domain proofs.

Deliverables, relative to the supplied workspace: P05.2-paper.tex; P05.2-paper.pdf; full argument.md; full notes.json; source-application-ledger.md; proof-audit.md; execution-requests.md; star-input.json; check_star_estimates.py; build_artifacts.py; record_provenance.py; evidence/star-check-output.json; evidence/build-summary.json; evidence/environment.json; evidence/provenance.json; and the actual source responses under sources/.

Observed checks. Exact Fraction arithmetic passed all 1,035 specified barycentric cases and 2,070 convex-function cases. The per-star counts were 36/72 for the cross, 972/1,944 for fine U(3,4), and 27/54 for the translated trivalent germ. Maximum sums of the other lower-combination coefficients were 3/4, 9/4 and 1. Inputs enumerate coefficients 0,1/64,…,8/64 and two convex functions per case. These are exhaustive finite results only for those lists. They do not certify the continuum proof or an MA domain. The final PDF has 13 pages; its final pdflatex pass exited zero without warnings. All 38 recorded artifact files matched their SHA-256 hashes. The preserved A224 and B225 source bodies also exactly matched the source hashes supplied in their harmless clarifications. These are provenance observations, not mathematical verification.
